title: Bialgebras induced by special left Alia algebras
author: Tianshui Ma, Chan Zhao, Huihui Zheng
description:
arXiv:2506.07061v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: This paper investigates bialgebraic structures associated with special left-Alia algebras. Based on the special left-Alia algebras originally introduced in the study of algebras with skew-symmetric identity of degree 3, we systematically examine the structure of a Nijenhuis left-Alia bialgebra. This bialgebra consists of a compatible pairing between a Nijenhuis left-Alia algebra and a Nijenhuis left-Alia coalgebra. We prove that a Nijenhuis special left-Alia bialgebra, which is constructed from a commutative associative algebra (or a cocommutative coassociative coalgebra) equipped with two commuting linear maps, can be induced from a Nijenhuis commutative cocommutative associative D-bialgebra. This establishes an explicit link between these two families of bialgebraic structures. Furthermore, the paper provides a general method for constructing Nijenhuis operators on arbitrary left-Alia algebras and coalgebras.

author: Haiying Li, Tianshui Ma
description:

title: A monoid-theoretical approach to infinite direct-sum decompositions of modules
author: Zahra Nazemian, Daniel Smertnig
description:
arXiv:2401.08203v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Let $\mathcal C$ be a class of modules over a ring $R$, closed under direct sums over index sets of cardinality $κ$ and isomorphisms, and such that the isomorphism classes form a set. The monoid of modules $V(\mathcal C)$ encodes the behavior of finite direct-sum decompositions of modules in $\mathcal C$. We endow $V(\mathcal C)$ with an additional operation reflecting $κ$-indexed direct sums, and study the resulting $κ$-monoid $V^κ(\mathcal C)$. The braiding-property and an equivalent universal property, allow us to show: if every module in $\mathcal C$ is a direct sum of at most $κ$ many modules generated by strictly fewer than $λ$ many elements, then all relations on $V^κ(\mathcal C)$ are induced by relations between direct sums indexed by sets of cardinality strictly less than $λ$. A theorem of Kaplansky states that every projective module is a direct sum of countably generated modules. We show that also all relations between infinite direct sums of projective modules are induced from those between countable direct sums of countably generated projective modules. If every projective module over a ring $R$ is a direct sum of finitely generated projective modules, then the monoid of finitely generated projective modules $V(R)$ completely determines the $κ$-monoid $V^κ(R)$. Together with the realization result of Bergman and Dicks, this characterizes the $κ$-monoids appearing as $V^κ(R)$ for a hereditary ring. In general, the $\aleph_0$-monoid $V^{\aleph_0}(R)$ fully determines $V^κ(R)$. Herbera and Příhoda's characterization of monoids of countably generated projective modules $V^*(R)$ over semilocal noetherian rings, yields a characterization of $V^κ(R)$ for these rings. We also characterize two-generated $\aleph_0$-monoids that appear as $V^{\aleph_0}(R)$ for hereditary rings $R$.

title: Differential equations as difference-differential equations
author: Wei Li, Thomas Scanlon
description:
arXiv:2610.22317v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We analyze the behavior of systems of algebraic differential equations when considered as systems of difference-differential equations, with special emphasis on systems which define minimal sets relative to the theory $\operatorname{DCF}$ of differentially closed fields of characteristic zero with $m$ distinguished commuting derivations. We show that if $p$ is a minimal type relative to $\operatorname{DCF}$ defined by a system of algebraic partial differential equations and inequations and the forking geometry on $p$ is trivial (also called ``disintegrated''), then $p$ remains minimal when regarded as a partial type relative to the theory $\operatorname{DCFA}$ of difference-differentially closed fields of characteristic zero with $m$ commuting derivations in the sense that every completion has $\operatorname{SU}$-rank one. We illustrate this theorem by describing in detail the possible difference-differential equations consistent with differential equations of the form $y' = y^3 + a_2 y^2 + a_1 y + a_0$ where $a_0$, $a_1$, and $a_2$ are differential constants.

title: Evolution algebras: a survey of results and a list of open problems
author: Ivan Kaygorodov, Cándido Martín González, Antonio Viruel
description:
arXiv:2610.22248v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evolution algebras, introduced by J. P. Tian as an algebraic model of non- Mendelian inheritance, are commutative algebras with a basis whose distinct elements multiply to zero. The first part of the paper surveys the theory: low-dimensional classifica- tions, structure theory, nilpotency, automorphisms and derivations, directed graphs and random walks, infinite-dimensional and dynamical aspects, and embedding theorems. The second part is a unified list of fifty open questions and eleven new conjectures, each accompanied by the available evidence; two of the conjectures and one of the questions are settled here. title: An infinite completely normal basis theorem
author: Patrik Lundström
description:
arXiv:2610.22247v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $L/K$ be an arbitrary Galois extension with group $G$, equipped with the Krull topology. Let $C(G,K)$ denote the $K$-vector space of continuous functions $G\to K$, with $K$ discrete and $G$ acting by left translation. We prove that there exists a $G$-equivariant $K$-linear isomorphism $\varphi:C(G,K)\to L$ such that, for every open subgroup $H$ of $G$, the map $\varphi^H:C(H,L^H)\to L$ induced by extension by zero and extension of scalars is an $H$-equivariant $L^H$-linear isomorphism. This gives a completely normal analogue of Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem; the case of finite base fields was previously established in an equivalent form by Hachenberger.

title: Direct products of Gorenstein flat modules over coherent rings
author: Guocheng Dai, Jiangsheng Hu
description:
arXiv:2610.22078v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We construct a commutative coherent local algebra of Krull dimension zero and a countably generated projectively coresolved Gorenstein flat module whose countable power has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. This answers negatively the question of whether Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring are closed under direct products. As a consequence, we obtain a pure-injective Ding injective module whose character module has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension and whose character bidual has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. We also give equivalent conditions for Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring to be closed under direct products, in terms of relative Mittag--Leffler conditions, stationarity, and Gorenstein flat and injective dimensions of character biduals. For the constructed ring, we exhibit a decreasing countable sequence of strong submodules of a free module whose intersection has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. Thus the abstract elementary class of Gorenstein flat modules, with the strong submodule relation, has finite character but does not admit intersections.

title: Ideals in Enveloping Algebras of Loop Algebras
author: Alexey V. Petukhov, Susan J. Sierra
description:
arXiv:2610.22040v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra, and consider the loop algebra $L\mathfrak g = \mathfrak g[s, s^{-1}]$ and the affine Lie algebra $\widehat{\mathfrak g}$, which is an extension of $L\mathfrak g$ by a central element $c$. It is known that the rings $\operatorname{U}(\widehat{\mathfrak g})/(c-λ)$ are simple for any nonzero scalar $λ$. On the other hand, the universal enveloping algebra $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g) \cong \mathrm{U}(\widehat{\mathfrak g})/(c)$ has many two-sided ideals, and in this paper we investigate their structure. We show that the two-sided structure of $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ is both intricate and well-behaved. Specifically, $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ does not satisfy the ascending chain condition on two-sided ideals, but the two-sided ideals still have a nice structure: there is a canonical nested collection of ideals $I_n$, parameterised by positive integers, so that any nonzero two-sided ideal of $\mathrm{U}(L\mathfrak g)$ contains all $I_n$ for $n \gg 0$. The ideals $I_n$ can be thought of as universal annihilators of natural classes of finite-dimensional representations of $L\mathfrak g$. We also study the Poisson structure of the symmetric algebra $\mathrm{S}(L\mathfrak g)$ and give applications to the representation theory of $L\mathfrak g$.

title: Automorphisms of Free Metabelian Lie Algebras, II
author: Ualbai Umirbaev
description:
arXiv:2610.21954v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We show that every automorphism of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ of rank $n\geq 4$ over an arbitrary field $K$ is almost tame; that is, it can be expressed as a product of Chein automorphisms (also called one-row transformations). Moreover, we prove that, for $n\geq 4$, the group $\mathrm{Aut}(M_n)$ of all automorphisms of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ over a field $K$ of characteristic not equal to $3$ is generated by its linear automorphisms, together with a single quadratic and a single cubic automorphism. The same result holds for fields of any characteristic if $n\geq 5$.

title: Modules and operator rings of Reynolds algebras
author: Jun He, Xiao-Song Peng, Chenghao Zhang, Yi Zhang
description:
arXiv:2610.21829v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We develop a module theory for weighted Reynolds algebras by constructing an associa?tive ring that records the algebra action and the module operator. The categories of left and right Reynolds modules are equivalent to the corresponding module categories over this ring, and their tensor products agree under these equivalences. We construct free Reynolds modules and give an explicit graded description of the operator ring for idempotent classical Reynolds operators fixing the identity. When the Reynolds operator on the algebra is bijective, modules with bijective module operators correspond to differential modules satisfying an invertibility condition. The operator ring transfers the Hom-tensor adjunction, Morita theory and derived functors to Reynolds modules. Explicit computations over a field show that the identity operator gives an operator ring of global dimension one, whereas the zero operator gives one of infinite global dimension.

title: Generalized Cluster Algebra Homomorphisms Induced by Cluster Tube Embeddings
author: Mingze Li
description:
arXiv:2610.21822v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We relate multiplication formulas for regular modules in coefficient-free acyclic affine cluster algebras with skew-symmetric exchange matrices to the imaginary exchange relations of Reading-Stella. Introducing a parameter $z$ into the construction of Zhou-Zhu, we define a weighted cluster character on cluster tubes that satisfies generalized exchange relations of type $C_{n-1}$ and yields a bijection between indecomposable rigid objects and cluster variables. Using the multiplication formulas and difference property of Ding-Xiao-Xu, we show that non-homogeneous tube embeddings induce injective homomorphisms into ordinary affine cluster algebras under $z\mapsto X_δ$. Comparison with Reading-Stella's relations identifies $X_δ$ with the corresponding theta function, giving a representation-theoretic interpretation of the generalized exchange parameter.

title: A proof of the interlacing conjecture for the singular values of Sylvester-Kac matrices
author: Fuying Tang, Shuo Shi
description:
arXiv:2610.21702v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Boros and Rózsa (Linear Algebra Appl. 421 (2007) 407--416) reduced the singular value problem for the odd-order Sylvester--Kac matrix $P\in\mathbb{R}^{(2m+1)\times(2m+1)}$ to those for $Q^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{(m+1)\times m}$ and $S^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times(m+1)}$ via a permutation similarity transformation. They noted that $(Q^{(m)})^{T}Q^{(m)}-S^{(m)}(S^{(m)})^{T}$ is positive definite, and also conjectured that $σ_i(S^{(m)})\geσ_{i+1}(Q^{(m)})$ for $1\le i\le m-1$ and $m\ge2$. In this paper, we prove that these inequalities are strict and establish the strict interlacing relation \begin{equation*} σ_1(Q^{(m)})>σ_1(S^{(m)})> \cdots>σ_m(Q^{(m)})> σ_m(S^{(m)})>0 \end{equation*} for all $m\ge1$. Here, $σ_i(\cdot)$ denotes the $i$-th largest singular value of a matrix.

title: Automorphisms of triality groups over local rings
author: Elena Bunina, Avi Berezovskiy, Deep Makadiya
description:
arXiv:2610.21662v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative local ring with $2,3\in R^\times$, and let $ρ\in\Aut(R)$ satisfy $ρ^3=\id$. We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full triality groups in the adjoint and simply connected forms of type $D_4$. Every automorphism is uniquely determined by an adjoint group element and a ring automorphism preserving the trace $T=\id+ρ+ρ^2$; conversely, every such pair defines an automorphism. A square-zero example shows that trace-preserving coefficient automorphisms need not normalize $\langleρ\rangle$ when $ρ$ is nontrivial on $R$ but trivial on its residue field. We also prove a relative rigidity theorem for homomorphisms from elementary triality groups over arbitrary coefficient rings to local targets with $2$ and $3$ invertible, assuming that an adjoint conjugation makes the parameter-one root images standard modulo the maximal ideal. Conversely, every unital trace-preserving ring homomorphism into such a local coefficient ring induces the corresponding homomorphism of elementary groups.

title: Star-Ordered Rotor Loops in Clifford Algebras
author: Nik Jenzer
description:
arXiv:2610.21593v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider, in a real Clifford algebra, a family of unit bivectors $B_i = C S_i$ formed from $k+1$ pairwise anticommuting generators $C, S_1, \ldots, S_k$ with square $-1$; we call this a \emph{star family} with \emph{central generator} $C$ and \emph{leaf generators} $S_i$. For the associated rotors $U_i(θ_i) = \cos\frac{θ_i}{2} + B_i \sin\frac{θ_i}{2}$ we study two objects: the ordered chain $P_k = U_1 \cdots U_k$ and the \emph{star-ordered rotor loop} $Θ_k = P_k \, Q_k$ with the \emph{same-order reversion product} $Q_k = \widetilde U_1 \cdots \widetilde U_k$, as opposed to the trivially reversed order, for which $U_1 \cdots U_k \widetilde U_k \cdots \widetilde U_1 = 1$. The scalar part of $Θ_k$ measures the \emph{order defect} of the family. We prove two theorems. First, the scalar part of the chain factorises, $\langle P_k \rangle_0 = \prod_{i=1}^k \cos\frac{θ_i}{2}$; this requires the star structure, and we give a counterexample. Second, we derive a closed expression for $\langle Θ_k \rangle_0$, valid for every $k$, whose coefficients obey a \emph{period-four sign law} $η(m) = (-1)^{\lfloor m/2 \rfloor}$ and which admits the compact form $\langle Θ_k \rangle_0 = \operatorname{Re}\!\big[(1-\mathrm{i}) \prod_i (\cos^2\frac{θ_i}{2} + \mathrm{i}\sin^2\frac{θ_i}{2})\big]$, holding for every pairwise anticommuting unit family without further hypothesis. From the compact form we obtain a polar form, a complete zero criterion, a lacunary coefficient rule, and a proof of non-separability for $k \geq 2$. Two supplementary theorems extend the result to arbitrary permutations of the index order and to families with mixed squares $B_i^2 \in \{-1, +1\}$. All proofs use only anticommutation, reversion and the symmetry of the scalar form; no physical interpretation is assumed or claimed.

title: A Krause-type recollement for Q-shaped derived categories
author: Yajun Ma, Peiru Yang
description:
arXiv:2610.21507v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Let k be a commutative noetherian hereditary ring and let Q be a small, Hom-finite, locally bounded k-linear category admitting a Serre functor and satisfying the strong retraction property, with nilpotent pseudo-radical. For every k-algebra A, we construct a recollement of the Q-shaped homo?topy category KQ(A Inj) of objectwise injective Q-shaped modules by its full subcategory Kac Q (A Inj) of exact objects and the Q-shaped derived category DQ(A). The construction uses complete hereditary cotorsion pairs and does not require A to be noetherian. title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality
author: Chengming Bai, Li Guo, Yunhe Sheng, You Wang
description:
arXiv:2610.21365v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replication for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$, with the property that an operation of $\opd$ splits into a negative sum of two or three operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd \to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, the process gives Manin black products, \[ \ABSu(\opd) \cong \antiprelie \bullet \opd, \qquad \ATSu(\opd)\cong \antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we introduce the anti-duplicator \(\ADup(\mathcal P)\) and anti-triplicator \(\ATrip(\mathcal P)\) and prove \[ \ADup(\opd^!)\cong \ABSu(\opd)^!, \qquad \ATrip(\opd^!)\cong \ATSu(\opd)^!. \] Consequently, the anti-duplicator gives a new way to calculate Manin white products. %, in particular, $\ADup(\opd)\cong \antiperm\circ\opd$. The framework recovers known anti-splittings, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie, and anti-pre-Poisson structures, in a uniform operadic form and produces further examples and dual pairs.

title: Zhang twists for semigroups and groupoids, with applications to Steinberg algebras
author: Roozbeh Hazrat, Zachary Mesyan, Benjamin Steinberg
description:
arXiv:2610.21005v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Zhang twists provide a powerful mechanism for deforming graded algebras, while preserving their graded module categories. We extend this theory by introducing Zhang twists for graded semigroups and graded ample groupoids. We show that the twisting construction preserves a broad class of semigroup structures, and that two graded monoids are twists of each other if and only if their categories of graded sets are pointedly equivalent. We show that Zhang twists are compatible with noncommutative Stone duality: twists on graded-Boolean inverse semigroups are in correspondence with those on the associated graded ample groupoids. Moreover, in the setting of Steinberg algebras we prove that twisting the groupoid gives the same result as twisting the corresponding algebra. These results provide a unified framework linking graded semigroups, inverse semigroup duality, ample groupoids, and graded algebras, while extending the scope of Zhang twists to settings arising from symbolic dynamics, graph algebras, and Steinberg algebras.

title: Two Short Proofs of the $A^A$ Theorem
author: George Grätze
description:
arXiv:2610.20802v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In 1984, D.~Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ implies $A\cong B$ for finite, nonempty ordered sets $A$ and~$B$. J.\,D. Farley and the author proved that it does. In this paper, we give two short proofs using all intervals of maximum height and the elements with exactly one lower cover. The first proof averages over these intervals; the second takes their disjoint sum and constructs three invariants. Both avoid the auxiliary ordering, direct factorization, and canonical coordinates of the earlier proof.

author: Christian Mehl
description:
arXiv:2610.20646v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper the generic behavior of the Jordan structure of symplectic matrices under low-rank structure-preserving transformations is considered. So far, only the case of rank-one perturbations was covered in the literature, and this result is now extended to the case of arbitrary rank $k$. As a key step toward the main result, it is shown that all symplectic matrices that differ from the identity by rank $k$ can be represented as a product of $k$ symplectic reflectors unless they are similar to a diagonalizable matrix having only the eigenvalues $\pm 1$.

description:

title: The $φ$-conjugation of quaternionic matrices and generalized Autonne-Takagi factorization
author: Cailing Yao, Bingzhe Hou, Yue Xin
description:
arXiv:2609.22825v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Let $φ$ be a quaternion of modulus $1$. In this article, we study some topics related to $φ$-conjugation for quaternionic matrices, including $φ$-Hermitian matrices, $φ$-conjugate normal matrices, unitary $φ$-congruence and $φ$-HSH decomposition (decomposition of a $φ$-Hermitian matrix and a skew $φ$-Hermitian matrix). In particular, we generalize the Autonne-Takagi factorization of quaternion $φ$-Hermitian matrices for all unit quaternion $φ$. This gives an affirmative answer to a problem proposed by R. Horn and F. Zhang in the paper ``A generalization of the complex Autonne-Takagi factorization to quaternion matrices, Linear Multilinear A. 60: 1239--1244, 2012''.

title: Orthogonal completion of algebraic systems II
author: A. Yu. Golubkov
description:

Abstract: The paper "Orthogonal completion of algebraic systems II" continues the line of "Orthogonal completion of algebraic systems" from the perspective of almost classical localizations of algebras and the conclusions of K.~I.~Beidar's doctoral dissertation. title: The ozone group of $U_q^+(B_2)$
author: James Gómez, Helbert Venegas
description:
arXiv:2609.04919v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We determine the ozone group of \(U_q^{+}(B_2)\). More precisely, if \(\ell=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)\) when \(q\) is a root of unity, we obtain $$ \operatorname{Oz}(U_q^{+}(B_2)) \cong \begin{cases} μ_2 , & \text{if \(q\) is not a root of unity},\\[2mm] μ_{\gcd(\ell,2)}, & \text{if \(q\) is a primitive \(m\)-th root of unity, \(m\geq5\).} \end{cases} $$ We also study several homological properties of \(U_q^{+}(B_2)\), showing that it is Artin--Schelter regular of global dimension \(4\), Auslander-regular, Cohen--Macaulay, strongly Noetherian, and skew Calabi--Yau. Using two different iterated Ore presentations, we show that its Nakayama automorphism is trivial for every $q \in \K^*$, so $U_q^{+}(B_2)$ is Calabi--Yau of dimension $4$; for $q$ not a root of unity this also follows from work of Goodearl and Yakimov. When $q$ is a primitive $m$-th root of unity with $m\geq5$, we deduce that the center is Gorenstein, we check directly that the ozone group acts with trivial homological determinant, and we describe the nonzero normal elements in terms of the ozone group.

title: Fusion rules from the Norton inequality
author: Alonso Castillo-Ramirez
description:
arXiv:2607.03237v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The Norton inequality is one of the fundamental axioms in the theory of Majorana and axial algebras, yet its precise structural consequences have remained only partially understood. In this paper, we show that the Norton inequality alone forces the $0$- and $1$-eigenspace fusion rules for arbitrary idempotents in a commutative real algebra $A$ equipped with a Frobenius form. More precisely, if the Frobenius form is nondegenerate (as in Majorana algebras), we prove that the eigenspaces $A_0(e)$ and $A_1(e)$ of an arbitrary idempotent $e \in A$ are subalgebras and annihilate one another: \[ A_0(e)A_1(e)=\{0\}, \] while in the degenerate case the corresponding inclusions hold modulo the radical of the Frobenius form. This answers a question of T. M. Mudziiri Shumba and S. Shpectorov concerning the closure of the $0$-eigenspace $A_0(e)$.

title: Quasi-projective dimensions of complexes over rings
author: Hongxing Chen, Jiangsheng Hu, Xiaoyan Yang
description:
arXiv:2604.09279v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Quasi-projective dimension of modules over associative rings is generalized in this paper to the one of complexes of modules. Basic properties of this dimension are established, including a comparison result with projective dimension and a derived Auslander-Buchsbaum formula for complexes of finite quasi-projective dimension. Several sufficient conditions are provided for a commutative noetherian local ring to be a complete intersection under the assumption that each finitely generated module has finite quasi-projective dimension. This provides some positive answers to an open question on quasi-projective dimension proposed by Gheibi-Jorgensen-Takahashi. Moreover, the behavior of quasi-projective dimension under taking the quotient of a commutative ring modulo a regular sequence is investigated, and some partial results toward the change-of-rings question on quasi-projective dimension are given.

title: Nonassociative algebras of anti-biderivation-type
author: Saïd Benayadi, Said Boulmane, Ivan Kaygorodov
description:
arXiv:2506.17228v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to study the class of Jacobi-Jordan-admissible algebras whose product is an anti-biderivation of the related Jacobi-Jordan algebra; we call them $\mathcal A{\rm BD}$-algebras. We give characterizations of $\mathcal A{\rm BD}$-algebras and show that this class includes Jacobi-Jordan algebras, symmetric anti-Leibniz algebras and anti-${\rm LR}$-algebras. The derived algebra of an anti-${\rm LR}$-algebra is associative and commutative, and all identities of its commutator algebra follow from the metabelian identity and one identity of degree $4$. We also study $\mathcal A$flexible ${\mathcal A}{\rm BD}$-algebras and prove that a complex finite-dimensional Jacobi-Jordan algebra admits a non-trivial post-Jacobi-Jordan structure if and only if its dimension is at least $3$. Finally, we give the algebraic classification of complex $3$-dimensional $\mathcal A{\rm BD}$-algebras and show that complex finite-dimensional simple ${\mathcal A}{\rm BD}$-algebras are anticommutative, while perfect ones need not be; the minimal dimension of perfect non-anticommutative ${\mathcal A}{\rm BD}$-algebras is $4$.

title: Polygraphic resolutions for operated algebras
author: Zuan Liu, Philippe Malbos
description:
arXiv:2502.16304v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: This paper introduces the structure of operated polygraphs as a categorical model for rewriting in operated algebras, generalizing Gröbner--Shirshov bases with non-monomial termination orders. We show how to construct polygraphic resolutions of free operated algebras from confluent and terminating presentations. We provide a combinatorial description of critical branchings of operated polygraphs using the structure of polyautomata introduced in this paper. Polyautomata are linear polygraphs equipped with an operator structure formalized by a pushdown automaton. Finally, we apply our constructions to several families of operated algebras, including Rota--Baxter algebras, differential algebras, and differential Rota--Baxter algebras.

title: On partial representations of pointed Hopf algebras
author: Arthur Rezende Alves Neto, Marcelo Muniz Alves, Eliezer Batista
description:
arXiv:2502.03642v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The theory of partial representations first appeared in the context of groups to deal with restrictions of representations to non-invariant subspaces. Partial representations of a group $G$ correspond to representations of a groupoid algebra constructed out of $G$. The notion of a partial representation can be extended to the context of Hopf algebras. For a Hopf algebra $H$, its partial representations correspond to representations of a Hopf algebroid $H_{par}$, also constructed out of data coming from $H$. In this work, we describe the structure of the algebra $H_{par}$ for $H$ being a pointed Hopf algebra with a finite group of grouplikes $G(H)$. This algebra can be explicitly written as a direct sum, reflecting the groupoid algebra associated to the group $G(H)$. Explicit examples of rank one Hopf algebras are done in the nilpotent and the non-nilpotent cases.

title: Approximation of graded bialgebras
author: Giovanna Carnovale, Francesco Esposito, Lleonard Rubio y Degrassi
description:
arXiv:2412.00234v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Motivated by an equivalence of categories established by Kapranov and Schechtman, we introduce, for each non-negative integer d, the category of connected bialgebras modulo d+1. We show that these categories fit into an inverse system of categories whose inverse limit category is equivalent to the category of connected bialgebras. In addition, we extend the notion of approximation of connected bialgebras to those that are not necessarily generated in degree 1 and show that, for connected bialgebras in the category of Yetter-Drinfeld modules over a Hopf algebra, approximation is compatible with cocycle twisting.

title: The zero divisor and augmentation conjectures for medial quandle rings
author: Luc Ta
description:
arXiv:2610.20306v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For quandle rings, Bardakov--Passi--Singh and Elhamdadi--Nunez--Singh respectively formulated an analogue of Kaplansky's zero divisor conjecture and a weakened analogue of Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture involving the augmentation map. In this note, we verify these conjectures for medial quandles. The latter holds for a larger class of quandles; we characterize integral domains over which the statement holds for this class. We also characterize integral domains of characteristic 0 over which the statement holds for a given finite Alexander quandle.

title: Identities and isomorphisms of finite graded matrix algebras
author: Diogo Diniz, Daniela Martinez Correa, Dimas José Gonçalves, Plamen Koshlukov
description:
arXiv:2610.20113v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a finite field and let $G$ be a group such that every finite subgroup of $G$ is cyclic. In this paper we classify the division gradings by cyclic groups on matrix algebras over $\mathbb{F}$. This yields the classification of the $G$-gradings on these algebras. Moreover if $G$ is abelian we prove that two matrix algebras over $\mathbb{F}$ with $G$-gradings satisfy the same graded identities if and only if they are isomorphic as graded algebras.

title: On the Fomin-Kirillov algebras
author: Yang Zhang
description:
arXiv:2610.20033v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Fomin-Kirillov algebras $\mathcal{FK}_n$ are shown to be infinite-dimensional for $n\geq 6$. By computer calculations, we find an explicit nonzero primitive element of degree 14 in the identity component of $\mathcal{FK}_6$. For every $n\geq 6$, the existence of such an element implies that $\mathcal{FK}_n$ contains a polynomial subalgebra and is therefore infinite-dimensional, and that the canonical homomorphism from $\mathcal{FK}_n$ onto its associated Nichols algebra is not an isomorphism.

title: Invariant factors from products of cyclotomic polynomials, with applications
author: Vanni Noferini, Gerald Williams
description:
arXiv:2610.19205v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $f,g\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be products of cyclotomic polynomials such that either $g/\gcd(f,g)$ or $f/\gcd(f,g)$ (or both) is squarefree. We give explicit formulae for the invariant factors of $f(C_g)$, where $C_g$ is the companion matrix of $g$, expressing them in terms of the indices and multiplicities of the cyclotomic factors of $f$ and $g$. A more compact formula holds for the circulant case $g(t)=t^n-1$, assuming that every cyclotomic factor shared by $f$ and $g$ has multiplicity $1$ in $f$. We discuss applications to several topics, including abelianizations of cyclically presented groups, homology groups of cyclic branched covers of knots, adjacency matrices and shifted graph Laplacians, $K$-theory, and Smith forms of matrix powers. For example, for two families of hyperbolic knots we give the first integral homology in every covering degree; or, when $g$ is squarefree, we determine the least eventual period of the Smith forms of powers of $f(C_g)$.

title: Exact sequences of representation categories of weak Hopf algebras
author: Quinn T. Kolt
description:
arXiv:2609.40298v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We study exact sequences of representation categories of weak Hopf algebras over an arbitrary field. Given a sequence $A\overset{k}{\to} B\oversetπ{\to} H$, where $A$ and $B$ are weak Hopf algebras and $H$ is a Hopf algebra, we develop verifiable algebraic conditions on $k$ and $π$ under which there is an exact sequence $\mathrm{Rep}(H)\to\mathrm{Rep}(B)\to\mathrm{Rep}(A)$ of tensor categories in the sense of Bruguières and Natale (2011). Along the way, we develop a generalization of the restriction of scalars functor for maps $π:B\to H$ between associative algebras satisfying a weakened multiplicativity constraint depending on a relatively separable subalgebra $B_r\subseteq B$, as well as a theory of kernels and cokernels for weak Hopf algebras. We, in particular, find that the cokernel of a weak Hopf algebra homomorphism $k:A\to B$ always exists, is a Hopf algebra, and the cokernel map is surjective when $A$ is connected. We conclude by studying examples of such exact sequences built from groupoids, formal ribbon extensions of quasitriangular weak Hopf algebras, and cocycled crossed products of a Hopf algebra acting weakly on a weak Hopf algebra.

title: Weak del Pezzo surfaces are characterized by the existence of $2$-tilting bundles
author: Ryu Tomonaga
description:
arXiv:2510.26199v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: For $d\geq1$, a tilting bundle on a regular proper $d$-dimensional variety over a field is called $d$-tilting if its endomorphism algebra has global dimension $d$, the smallest possible value. We prove that, over any field, the existence of a $d$-tilting bundle implies that the anticanonical bundle is semiample and big, and hence the variety is weak Fano. Moreover, the endomorphism algebra is $d$-representation tame. Conversely, every weak del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic admits a $2$-tilting bundle. Thus a smooth projective surface over such a field admits a $2$-tilting bundle if and only if it is a weak del Pezzo surface. This proves the variety case of Chan's conjecture, originally formulated in characteristic zero, and extends it to arbitrary characteristic. As an application, we construct a non-commutative crepant resolution (NCCR) of the anticanonical ring of any regular proper $d$-dimensional variety over any field admitting a $d$-tilting bundle. The NCCR is the endomorphism algebra of the pulled-back bundle on the total space of the canonical bundle. In particular, we obtain NCCRs of anticanonical cones over Du Val del Pezzo surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. These NCCRs are the $3$-Calabi--Yau completions of the endomorphism algebras of $2$-tilting bundles on the minimal resolutions, extending the known construction for smooth del Pezzo surfaces to the Du Val case.

As an application, we construct a non-commutative crepant resolution (NCCR) of the anticanonical ring of any regular proper $d$-dimensional variety over any field admitting a $d$-tilting bundle. The NCCR is the endomorphism algebra of the pulled-back bundle on the total space of the canonical bundle. In particular, we obtain NCCRs of anticanonical cones over Du Val del Pezzo surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. These NCCRs are the $3$-Calabi--Yau completions of the endomorphism algebras of $2$-tilting bundles on the minimal resolutions, extending the known construction for smooth del Pezzo surfaces to the Du Val case.

title: Artin-Schelter Gorenstein property of Hopf Galois extensions
author: Ruipeng Zhu
description:
arXiv:2501.02828v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: This paper investigates the homological properties of the faithfully flat Hopf Galois extension $A \subseteq B$. It establishes that when $B$ is a noetherian affine PI algebra and $A$ is AS Gorenstein, $B$ inherits the AS Gorenstein property. Furthermore, we demonstrate that injective dimension serves as a monoidal invariant for AS Gorenstein Hopf algebras. Specifically, if two such Hopf algebras have equivalent monoidal categories of comodules, then their injective dimensions are equal.

title: $δ$-derivations of simple finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras
author: Ivan Kaygorodov
description:
arXiv:1010.2419v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We describe non-trivial $δ$-derivations of semisimple finite-dimensional Jordan algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic not $2$, and of simple finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. For these classes of algebras and superalgebras, non-zero non-trivial $δ$-derivations are shown to be missing for $δ\notin\{ 0,\frac12,1\}$, and we give a complete account of $\frac12$-derivations.

title: Classification of $3$-dimensional unital commutative algebras
author: Maqpal Eraliyeva, Ivan Kaygorodov
description:
arXiv:2610.18689v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present the complete classification of non-isomorphic complex $3$-dimensional unital commutative algebras. Every such algebra decomposes canonically as $\mathbb Ce_1\oplus V$, where $e_1$ is the unit and $V$ is the kernel of the trace form; the induced traceless $2$-dimensional commutative algebra on $V$ is one of four algebras, and the classification reduces to the classification of symmetric bilinear forms on $V$ up to the automorphisms of this kernel. The answer consists of six algebras, three one-parameter families, one two-parameter family and one three-parameter family.

title: Okubo algebras and Exceptional Periodicity: tetracode gradings, root-lattice obstructions and Clifford cones
author: Alessio Marrani, Daniele Corradetti
description:
arXiv:2610.18643v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Okubo algebra brings together ternary gradings, integral root frames and rank-three geometry. We examine how these structures extend to the complex Exceptional Periodicity algebras. With $N=4(n+1)$, a tetracode character gives eight nonzero homogeneous components of dimension $t_n=8n+3+2^{4n}$. On a tip, a compatible grading has zero component of dimension $8n-5$ and eight nonzero components of dimension $1+2^{4n-3}$. The arithmetic behaves differently: for $n\geq2$, the lattice $D_N^+$ has no full-rank orthogonal frame of unscaled $A_2$ lattices. We exhibit failures of the Jacobi and Jordan identities and determine the derivations and full automorphism group of the ambient algebra above level one. We also give a Clifford-module proof, with the normalization fixed by root products, of the published realization of EP tips as special Vinberg $H$-algebras. This identifies a positive real form and yields explicit formulas for its cone, cubic, Cholesky coordinates and rational dual invariant. The cone is symmetric exactly at $n=1$. Its determinant-one hypersurface belongs to the known $L(8n,1,0)$ series, whose $r$- and $c$-maps give homogeneous scalar manifolds for supergravity theories with eight real supercharges.

title: Endochain Conditions on Modules and $p$-quasi-Frobenius Rings
author: Theophilus Gera, Amit Sharma, Manoj Kumar Patel, Pramod Kanwar
description:
arXiv:2610.18492v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Analogous to quasi-Frobenius rings, dual rings, and Johns rings, the classes of $p$-quasi-Frobenius rings, $p$-dual rings, $p$-Johns rings are introduced and used to discuss and settle principal analogues of the Faith-Menal, Faith, and FGF conjectures. A chain symmetry theorem establishes that for quasi-injective semi-projective modules with semiprime endomorphism ring, endonoetherianity and endoartinianity are equivalent and force the endomorphism ring to be semisimple artinian. Within this unified setting, it is shown that (1) two-sided $p$-Johns rings are $p$-quasi-Frobenius, giving a principal Faith-Menal analogue, with a counterexample showing that the one-sided hypothesis is insufficient; (2) semiprimary principal right ideal rings that are right principally injective and right Kasch are $p$-quasi-Frobenius-this affirmatively answers a question of Faith (Q2) in the principal two-sided ideal ring case and settles the principal Faith conjecture, with a counterexample showing the hypotheses to be indispensable; and (3) right $p$-Johns rings that are left CF and left perfect are $p$-quasi-Frobenius, yielding a principal FGF analogue, with a counterexample demonstrating that the hypotheses are essential. Wherever needed, examples are provided to show that various classes introduced are different from the existing classes in the literature.

title: Actions in varieties of non-associative algebras: a survey
author: Manuel Mancini
description:
arXiv:2610.18302v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: This article surveys the main results on the representability of internal actions in varieties of non-associative algebras over a field. We begin by recalling the general framework of internal actions and split extensions in semi-abelian categories, before specialising to Orzech categories of interest and varieties of non-associative algebras. We discuss action representability, weak action representability, and action accessibility, with emphasis on the relationship between the latter two notions. We then describe the constructions of the universal strict general actor in Orzech categories of interest and the external weak actor in action accessible, operadic varieties of non-associative algebras over a field, as well as their role in the study of weak action representability. We also give a tensor-domain formulation of partial algebras and adapt the construction of the external weak actor to this setting. These notions are illustrated by examples arising from associative, Lie, Leibniz, Jacobi-Jordan, anti-commutative anti-associative, alternative, and $2$-nilpotent algebras. We conclude with a summary of the known results and some open questions for future research.

title: Standard identities for polynomial vector fields
author: Nurtas Shyntas
description:
arXiv:2610.18149v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $W_n$ be the Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields in $n$ variables over a field of characteristic zero, and let $s_k$ denote the alternating sum of compositions of $k$ vector fields. The identity $s_{n^2+2n-1}=0$ has been asserted for arbitrary $n$. We give an explicit counterexample in dimension five, verified by an exact integer computation of a $34$-commutator. Together with the known vanishing of $s_{35}$, this shows that $35$ is the least degree of a standard identity on $W_5$. We then prove that $s_{n^2+2n-1}=0$ for every even $n\geq2$. The proof uses Lie algebra homology with coefficients in the polynomial algebra modulo constants and a lemma on invariant tensors. We describe the computation and provide the source code and verification results.

title: Actions of central Morita monoidal groupoids, and seven term exact sequences of all types
author: Ammu Elizabeth Antony, Yuval Ginosar
description:
arXiv:2610.18101v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce a strict monoidal groupoid associated with a given commutative ring $K$. It acts on the Clifford extension systems of $K$-central algebras which are graded by a group $G$, as well as on the generalized collective characters, both of type $φ\in$ Hom$(G,$ Aut$(K))$. These actions partition the two sets above with respect to graded Morita equivalence. By that we establish a seven term exact sequence of type $φ$, which boils down to the celebrated Chase-Harrison-Rosenberg sequence when $φ$ is Galois.

title: Zero divisors in group algebras of torsion-free groups in odd characteristic
author: S. V. Ivanov
description:
arXiv:2610.17662v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: A recent preprint constructs a finitely presented torsion-free group $G$ with a finite two-dimensional classifying space such that $\mathbb F_2[G]$ contains nonzero zero divisors. We extend this to every odd prime $p$: there is a finitely presented torsion-free group $G_p$, again with a finite two-dimensional classifying space, such that $\mathbb F_p[G_p]$ contains nonzero elements $α,β$ with $αβ=0$. Together with the case $p=2$, Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture therefore fails over every field of positive characteristic. The new ingredients are a signed version of the parity cancellation, made possible by a bipartite random model on one side; a type design built from the projective plane over $\mathbb F_{p^3}$ with $p$ additional letters, which makes every cross-intersection congruent to $1$ modulo $p$; and a squared-word decay estimate for this design, proved with an explicit test vector. The geometric part of the argument is taken from the characteristic-two construction. The characteristic-zero case remains open.

title: On the Real Waring Rank of a Biharmonic Form
author: Hua-Lin Huang, Yiming Liu, Yilun Tang
description:
arXiv:2610.17565v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop an effective method for determining the real Waring rank and the real border rank of biharmonic binary forms. By means of real apolarity, we convert both of these problems into membership questions for regions bounded by a hypocycloid and an epicycloid. We further provide a computable algebraic criterion for the relevant memberships, which involves only the signs of certain real-valued resultants.

title: Orthogonality of Defect Ideals for Jordan Homomorphisms
author: Cao Minh Nam
description:
arXiv:2610.17518v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $\varphi\colon A\to B$ be a Jordan homomorphism of associative algebras over a field $\mathbb{F}$ of characteristic different from $2$, with defect ideals $V_{\varphi}$ and $W_{\varphi}$. If $A=\operatorname{Alg}([[A,A],[A,A]])$, then $V_{\varphi}W_{\varphi}=W_{\varphi}V_{\varphi}=0$ and $V_{\varphi}\cap W_{\varphi}\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}(\operatorname{Alg}(\varphi(A)))$. Moreover, the induced map modulo $V_{\varphi}\cap W_{\varphi}$ is standard. The annihilator bound is sharp, even in finite dimension. As an application, when $A$ is unital and $A=K(A)$, every Jordan homomorphism defined on $A$ is splittable and standard. In this setting, the corresponding result of Brešar and Zelmanov holds without the surjectivity hypothesis.

title: Linear Laurent phenomenon algebras are of finite type
author: Oliver Daisey
description:
arXiv:2610.17441v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Laurent phenomenon algebras generalise cluster algebras by allowing irreducible exchange polynomials in place of binomials. Lam and Pylyavskyy proved finite type for those arising from graphs and conjectured that the same holds for every Laurent phenomenon algebra admitting a linear seed. We prove this conjecture over an arbitrary unique factorisation domain. Our proof constructs a nonzero element of the upper algebra divisible by every cluster variable. Comparing noninitial cluster variables with the prime factors of this element in the initial Laurent ring bounds the number of cluster variable classes and yields a finite normalised mutation pattern.

title: Group gradings, graded identities and central polynomials of algebras with almost polynomial $δ$-growth
author: Wesley Quaresma Cota, Daniela Martinez Correa
description:
arXiv:2610.17408v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The finite-dimensional $F$-algebras $D=F(e_{11}+e_{33})+Fe_{22}+Fe_{12}+Fe_{13}+Fe_{23} \subseteq UT_3$ and $D_0=Fe_{22}+Fe_{33}+Fe_{12}+Fe_{13}+Fe_{14}+Fe_{23}+Fe_{24}+Fe_{34} \subseteq UT_4$ occupy a distinguished position in the theory of central polynomials. Together with the infinite-dimensional Grassmann algebra, these algebras generate the only varieties of almost polynomial growth of proper central codimensions. We determine finite generating sets for their $T$-spaces of central polynomials and compute their central and proper central codimensions. We also prove that every group grading on $D_0$ is isomorphic to an elementary grading and determine the identities and codimensions associated with all its $\mathbb{Z}_2$-gradings.

title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
author: Marino Gran, James R. A. Gray
description:
arXiv:2610.17389v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest.

title: A Gordon--Green-type result for Gorenstein-projective modules
author: A. M. Bouhada, M. Laaraj
description:
arXiv:2610.17357v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let \(Λ\) be a \(\Z\)-graded Artin algebra which is Iwanaga--Gorenstein. We prove that \(Λ\) is CM-finite if and only if the category of gradable Gorenstein-projective modules has finite type, and if and only if the lengths of the indecomposable gradable Gorenstein-projective modules are bounded. Moreover, if \(Λ\) is CM-finite, then every Gorenstein-projective \(Λ\)-module is gradable. These results provide Gorenstein-projective analogues of the corresponding theorems of Gordon--Green for graded Artin algebras of finite representation type.

title: Proper varieties of distributive l-pregroups are periodic
author: Nikolaos Galatos, Simon Santschi
description:
arXiv:2610.16775v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We show that every proper variety of distributive $\ell$-pregroups is periodic; as a result, the subvariety lattice of the variety of distributive $\ell$-pregroups decomposes into a disjoint union of bounded intervals each consisting of all properly $n$-periodic varieties, for different $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$. On the way, we study non-periodic (one-generated) subalgebras of $\mathbf{F}(\mathbb{Z})$ and show that they either contain a non-periodic idempotent or they contain idempotents of arbitrary big periodicity. The same results holds for non-periodic one-generated subalgebras of $\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{J} \overrightarrow{\times} \mathbb{Z})$, where $\mathbf{J}$ is a chain, generated by a composite element and the resulting idempotents can be taken to be local in the associated wreath product.

title: Superdecomposable Complete Path Algebras
author: Can Hatipoğlu, Christian Lomp
description:
arXiv:2610.16746v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generalizing the setting of the second author's work on indecomposable modules without nonzero hollow factors, we characterize quivers $Q$ for which the dual algebra $R$ of the path coalgebra of $Q$, equivalently the complete path algebra, has no nonzero uniform right ideals: this happens exactly when every vertex of $Q$ can reach a vertex emitting at least two distinct arrows. Equivalently, the injective hull $E(R)$ of the right regular module is superdecomposable. These conditions are also equivalent to the path coalgebra having no nonzero hollow factor modules as a left module over its dual algebra.

title: Universal Varieties for Signatures of Membranes
author: Carlos Améndola, Gabriel Riffo, Leonard Schmitz
description:
arXiv:2610.16724v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Membranes are sufficiently smooth vector-valued functions defined on the unit square, widely used in applications such as interpolation of image data. The signature of a membrane is a collection of nonlinear features that capture its essential geometry. We index these features in the graded Hopf algebra of two-parameter shuffle products and study the algebraic varieties for each graded component. At each truncation level, we obtain the dimension of this variety via a novel Witt-type formula. We propose a Chen-Chow theorem for membranes, provably at the second truncation level, and conjecturally for higher levels with extensive computational evidence in the computer algebra system OSCAR.

title: Spectra and Support Theory for Wide Subcategories in $n$-Abelian Categories
author: Zheng Xin
description:
arXiv:2610.16541v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We develop a support theory for wide subcategories of essentially small Krull--Schmidt \(n\)-abelian categories. We construct spectra associated with families of wide subcategories and establish the corresponding support and radical theories. In particular, we characterize prime wide subcategories as the completely meet-irreducible elements of the lattice of wide subcategories and prove that every wide subcategory is recovered from the prime wide subcategories containing it. We further show that any classifying support datum is recovered, together with its object supports, from the canonical prime spectrum. title: Axioms and internal rigidity of spectral duality structures
author: Juan Antonio Vega Coso
description:
arXiv:2610.16454v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Spectral duality structures (SDS) explain why a distinguished family of initial distributions makes the absorption probabilities of resetting processes insensitive to the resetting mechanism. Here we study their axioms. We prove that the six defining conditions are mutually independent and determine what each one contributes. The key tool is a structure theorem valid for an arbitrary permutation and an arbitrary positive weight: every insensitive distribution is supported on a union of cycles balanced at a common level, and the level of a cycle is fixed by the geometric mean of the weight on it. From it, positivity selects the admissible root, the constant orbit product is equivalent to the existence of an insensitive distribution of full support, and the involution is equivalent to the response rank being equal to the number of free weight parameters. Without the duality relation, insensitivity of a single distribution is cheap and generically isolated; duality turns it into structural neutrality of the separatrix. The full-rank condition splits into two layers: a weaker condition is equivalent to maximal response rank, while full rank also excludes insensitivity at any other level. We then show that a single SDS is internally rigid: compatible semigroup structures force a constant weight, compatible abelian group structures obey a precise arithmetic condition, congruences form a simple lattice, and the automorphism group is computed explicitly. Finally, the axioms do not determine the orientation of the response; in the two-site case we give the exact condition under which the geometric and analytic sign criteria agree.

title: Double circulant LCD codes over $\mathbb{F}_2+u\mathbb{F}_2$ and constructions for binary LCD codes
author: Xingxing Xu, Minjia Shi, Jon-Lark Kim
description:
arXiv:2610.16121v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/4)$ from below. More importantly from the constructive viewpoint, by combining Gray images with a known extension construction, we obtain a binary LCD code with parameters $[29,15,7]$ and construct two explicit permutation-inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters $[45,23,9]$.

title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and the real Nullstellensatz for modules and sheaves
author: Jakob Cimprič
description:
arXiv:2610.15887v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We prove the geometric halves of Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and of the real Nullstellensatz for submodules of finitely generated modules and for coherent sheaves, complementing our earlier result that semiprime (resp. real) submodules are intersections of prime (resp. real prime) submodules. First, we pass from prime to maximal submodules: over a Jacobson ring, a prime submodule $P$ of $M$ is an intersection of maximal submodules whenever $M/P$ is a torsionless $R/(P:M)$-module, in particular whenever $M/P$ is finitely generated (the latter case is due to Maani Shirazi and Sharif). Consequently, if $R$ is a finitely generated algebra over an algebraically closed field and $M$ is finitely generated, the smallest semiprime submodule containing a submodule $N$ of $M$ consists of all $f\in M$ such that, for every point $a$, the value $f(a)$ (i.e. the image of $f$ in the fibre $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$) lies in $N(a)$ (i.e. the image of $N$ in $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$). We prove the real analogues over real Jacobson rings; for finitely generated algebras over a real closed field they are determined by the real points. The module classifications and directional vanishing formulas yield both Nullstellensätze for coherent sheaves on schemes of finite type over a field. We also prove compatibility of semiprimeness, reality and both radicals with arbitrary localization, and the resulting stalk criteria.

title: Semiprime and real submodules of arbitrary modules are intersections of prime and real prime submodules
author: Jakob Cimprič
description:
arXiv:2610.15869v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A submodule $N$ of an $R$-module $M$ is semiprime if $m\in(N:m)M$ implies $m\in N$. It is known that every semiprime submodule of $R^n$ is an intersection of prime submodules, and Aryapoor extended this to finitely generated modules. We show that no finiteness assumption is needed: every semiprime submodule of an \emph{arbitrary} $R$-module is the intersection of the prime submodules containing it. The proof is short and uses neither coordinates nor presentations; its key step is that a nonzero element $q$ of a semiprime module $Q$ satisfies $sq\notin\p Q$ for all $s\notin\p$, where $\p$ is any minimal prime over the annihilator of $q$. We define an $R$-module $M$ to be real if $\sum_i m_i\otimes m_i=0$ in $M\otimes_RM$ implies $m_i=0$ for all $i$, and a submodule $N\subseteq M$ real if the module $M/N$ is real. We prove the corresponding result for real submodules: every real submodule of an arbitrary module is the intersection of the real prime submodules containing it. On $R^n$ our notion of realness coincides with the coordinate definition used in earlier work on real Nullstellensätze for free modules.

title: The operad of anti-pre-Lie algebras and its Lie elements
author: Chengming Bai, Vladimir Dotsenko, Guilai Liu, Hongjie Wang
description:
arXiv:2610.15858v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We initiate a systematic operadic approach to anti-pre-Lie algebras. We study the operad controlling anti-pre-Lie algebras, its relationship to the operad of Novikov algebras and its cyclic structure. We establish that the Lie bracket of an anti-pre-Lie algebra satisfies the standard identity of degree five. We also establish a quadratic maximality property of the anti-pre-Lie operad with respect to this identity. We then show that the anti-pre-Lie operad and its Koszul dual are not Koszul and give a full description of the latter. Finally, we identify the Lie elements in the Koszul dual operad with the operad of metabelian Lie algebras.

title: Lie Algebras of Locally Finite Derivations over Fields of Positive Characteristic
author: Oksana Bezushchak, Anatoliy Petravchuk
description:
arXiv:2610.15731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic, and let $A$ be a finitely generated commutative associative $F$-algebra. We study Lie subalgebras of $Der \, A$ generated by locally finite derivations. We prove that if all commutators of the generators satisfy a natural local finiteness condition, then the associative subalgebra of $End_{F}\, A$ generated by these derivations is finite-dimensional.

title: On a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type
author: Hideto Asashiba, Ayako Itaba, Manuel Saorin
description:
arXiv:2610.15517v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We consider a family $(Λ_λ)_{λ\in \Bbbk^\times}$ of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type over an algebraically closed field $\Bbbk$, where $\Bbbk^\times:= \Bbbk\setminus \{0\}$, and for each $λ\in \Bbbk^\times$, $Λ_λ$ is socle equivalent to $Λ_1$, which is the trivial extension of a hereditary algebra of type $\tilde{A}$. We compute their Hochschild cohomologies, which shows that $Λ_λ$ is not derived equivalent to $Λ_1$ if $λ\neq 1$. This means that a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type given by Bocian--Holm--Skowro{\' n}ski is not complete.

title: A noetherian Hopf algebra has bijective antipode
author: Andrea Sciandra
description:
arXiv:2610.15473v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that a Hopf algebra over an arbitrary field has a bijective antipode if either its left or right regular module has finite uniform dimension. In particular, this solves Skryabin's conjecture, posed in 2006, that every noetherian Hopf algebra has a bijective antipode. Starting from Skryabin's injectivity theorem for weakly finite Hopf algebras, we associate to each finite-dimensional subcoalgebra an essential left ideal of common denominators that is also a right coideal in the antipode image. An annihilator identity makes this image essential in the original algebra as a left module over the image, yielding finite left uniform dimension from finite right uniform dimension. A second denominator construction inside the antipode image, together with a restricted inverse-antipode identity, proves surjectivity.

title: Bimodule duality and Artin's problem for skew field extensions
author: Niels Lauritzen, Jesper Funch Thomsen
description:
arXiv:2610.15469v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Emil Artin asked whether the left and right dimensions of an extension of skew fields must agree. Cohn and Schofield gave counterexamples through elaborate constructions. It has been a long-standing open question whether there is any division ring, infinite-dimensional over its center, for which the left and right indices agree whenever at least one is finite. We give the first such examples. Call a division ring index-symmetric if every division subring with at least one finite index has equal finite indices. Using a duality formula for bimodules over division algebras, we prove that every twisted Calabi--Yau division algebra is index-symmetric. The examples include the Weyl skew fields and, more generally, the quotient division rings of rings of differential operators on smooth affine varieties in characteristic zero. Further examples are the quotient division rings of enveloping algebras of finite-dimensional Lie algebras, Ore extensions of twisted Calabi--Yau noetherian domains, quantum affine spaces, and group algebras of torsion-free polycyclic-by-finite groups.

title: Cohen-Macaulay truncated path and Nakayama algebras
author: Takahiro Honma, Satoshi Usui
description:
arXiv:2610.15386v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper characterizes Cohen-Macaulay algebras in the sense of Auslander and Reiten [Progr. Math. 95(1991)] within the following two classes of finite dimensional algebras: (i) truncated path algebras and (ii) Nakayama algebras. For the former, our characterization in terms of ordinary quivers shows that if a Cohen-Macaulay truncated path algebra $Λ$ is connected, then $Λ$ or $D(Λ)$ gives a dualizing module, where $D$ denotes the standard duality. For the latter, we show that every Cohen-Macaulay Nakayama algebra $Λ$ is Iwanaga-Gorenstein. In particular, $Λ$ always gives a dualizing module. Consequently, there is no non-trivial Cohen-Macaulay algebra among truncated path and Nakayama algebras.

title: A categorical approach to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter equation
author: A. L. Agore, A. Chirvasitu, G. Militaru
description:
arXiv:2610.15347v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We investigate set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation from a categorical perspective. The paper has two main objectives. On the one hand, several existing constructions and classification results in the literature are recast in categorical terms, thereby showing that certain hypotheses previously imposed on such solutions are in fact superfluous. On the other hand, the categorical approach leads naturally to new classes of Yang-Baxter solutions. Our approach consists in identifying suitable subcategories of the category $\mathcal{YB}$ of Yang-Baxter solutions and providing categorical characterisations of the solutions they encode. As an application, we prove that the category of Płonka bi-magmas is isomorphic to the subcategory of $\mathcal{YB}$ consisting of solutions of the Baaj-Long-Skandalis equation. Along the way, we introduce and study a new class of Lyubashenko type solutions and examine the extent to which non-degenerate bijective solutions of the braid equation arise from skew left braces.

title: Local coherence and recollement of abelian categories
author: Mikhail Dusman, Alexander Pavlov
description:
arXiv:2610.14931v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We study how local coherenAAce of abelian categories behaves under gluing. For AB5 locally finitely presentable abelian categories, we give conditions on the gluing functors under which local coherence is transferred along a gluing $(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}, \mathcal{C})$: from $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}$, and conversely from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{A}$ or $\mathcal{C}$. The coherence theorem for augmented homotopes of Bondal and Zhdanovskiy is recovered as a special case, the coherence theorem for trivial extensions of Fossum, Griffith, and Reiten is a companion result in the same direction. We also introduce quasiprojective pairs of adjoint functors and prove a coherence criterion that generalises the criterion of Gomez Pardo and Martinez Hernandez to arbitrary Grothendieck categories. Finally, we extend Stenstr{ö}m's characterisation of coherence via FP-injective modules to compactly assembled Grothendieck categories: such a category is coherently assembled if and only if the class of CM-injective objects, defined through compact morphisms, is closed under filtered colimits. Along the way we revisit the various equivalent conditions for the coherence of a ring, collecting them in a single place. The proofs make use of the compactly assembled categories of Efimov.

title: A smooth non-compactly generated category
author: Alexander Frolov
description:
arXiv:2610.14874v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Let $A=\mathbb{Q}[t^{\frac{1}{2^n}}:n\geq 0]$ and consider $A[u,u^{-1};σ]$, a skew Laurent polynomial ring, where $σ(t^q)=t^{2q}$. We study the kernel of derived extension of scalars along $ A[u,u^{-1};σ]\longrightarrow\mathbb{Q}[u,u^{-1}], $ the quotient by $\mathfrak{m}A[u,u^{-1};σ]$, with $\mathfrak{m}=(t^{\frac{1}{2^n}}:n\geq 0)$. A finite free resolution of $\mathfrak{m}A[u,u^{-1};σ]$ over $ A[u,u^{-1};σ]\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} \bigl(A[u,u^{-1};σ]\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}} $ proves smoothness. A specialization inequality for matrix ranks supplies a nonzero exact colimit-preserving functor that vanishes on every compact object, proving failure of compact generation.

title: A Countable Three-Generated Orthomodular Lattice with No $σ$-Complete Embedding
author: Joaquim Reizi Higuchi
description:
arXiv:2610.14859v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We give an explicit countably infinite orthomodular lattice generated by three specified elements and a direct argument that it admits no injective homomorphism into any $σ$-complete orthomodular lattice. In particular, it does not embed into any set-sized complete orthomodular lattice. The source is a generated subalgebra of a cofinite reduced product of finite-dimensional real subspace lattices. A nonzero finite term $a$ is orthogonal to the orbit of a terminal line under every finite word in three Sasaki projections, while another finite term $X$ satisfies $π_aπ_X(t)=a$. If the image of this countable orbit has a supremum in a target orthomodular lattice, Sasaki adjunction forces that supremum to commute with the generator images. This forces the image of $a$ to vanish. The proof imposes no atomicity, modularity, Hilbert representation, cardinality bound on the target, or preservation of source infinitary operations. All target lemmas are derived from the orthomodular axioms.

title: Rota-Baxter operators and factorization of Lie affgebras
author: JiaJia Han, Abror Khudoyberdiyev, Yunzhou Xie, Yi Zhang
description:
arXiv:2610.14838v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce Rota-Baxter operators on Lie affgebras by an identity independent of the choice of origin and prove that they induce descendant Lie affgebra structures. We establish a bijection between ordered affine Lie factorizations and idempotent operators split at a chosen idempotent fixed point. A cokernel obstruction determines the existence of this point, while invariance under the structural endomorphisms characterizes splitting. We also determine when weighted descendants satisfy the affine Jacobi identity and when operators of nonzero weight give affine doubles. For canonical Lie affgebras, we describe all affine Rota-Baxter operators by Lie subalgebra decompositions and translation vectors, and classify them up to automorphism in dimensions at most two.

title: Diagonalization of skew-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices and $φ$-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices
author: Cailing Yao, Bingzhe Hou
description:
arXiv:2610.14692v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this article, we present the diagonalization of skew-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices in the sense of unitary equivalence. For a unit quaternion $φ$, we also obtain the diagonalization result of $φ$-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices in the sense of unitary $φ$-congruence, which generalizes the Autonne--Takagi factorization of symmetric complex matrices and $φ$-Hermitian quaternion matrices.

title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
author: Pavel Chebotarev
description:
arXiv:2610.14100v2 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $Λ_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $Λ_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partialΛ_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question remains open. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{π^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $Λ_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.

author: Mengya Yue, Xiaolei Shao
description:

Abstract: We prove that the three-element flat semiring $S_7$ is strongly nonfinitely based within the class of additively idempotent semirings. title: Linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant. An enhanced approach
author: Andrey Yurkov
description:
arXiv:2610.14060v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The discriminant of a square matrix is defined as a discriminant of its characteristic polynomial. In this paper we provide a description of linear maps preserving the matrix discriminant assuming that the ground field is large enough. Our description generalizes the known results to the case where the field may have a finite cardinality and its characteristic may divide the size of considered matrices. To obtain this description, we extend the approach used in our previous work on the subject and, in addition to that, introduce new invariants for the action of all bijective linear maps preserving a given polynomial, which are on independent interest and could be applied to other problems in the theory of linear preservers.

title: Hereditary NC Polynomials & Positivity Domains
author: Abdellah Islam, Jurij Volčič, Hugo J. Woerdeman
description:
arXiv:2610.14053v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Noncommutative polynomials, elements of the free algebra generated by several noncommuting variables $x_1,...,x_g,x_1^*,...,x_g^*$, are of importance in noncommutative algebra, free analysis and real algebraic geometry. We allow matrix coefficients and view these noncommutative polynomials as functions in several size-free matrix variables. The free locus of a noncommutative polynomial $f$ is the sequence of hypersurfaces $\mathscr{Z}_n(f)=\{X\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^g:\det f(X) = 0\}$. When $f$ is Hermitian, the positivity domain of $f$ is the sequence of semialgebraic sets $\mathcal{D}_n(f)=\{X\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^g:f(X)\text{ is positive semidefinite}\}$. We show for well-behaved cases that the Euclidean boundary of the positivity domain is Zariski dense in the free locus. This leads to a certificate for equality of positivity domains of coefficient-irreducible unsignatured atomic quadratics. Finally, we describe the geometric structure of positivity domains of hereditary quadratic polynomials through $Γ$-convexity.

title: $n$-Valued Analogue of Abel's Theorem
author: Mikhail Kornev
description:
arXiv:2610.14044v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Abel's classical theorem shows that a continuously differentiable one-dimensional associative law with a two-sided unit is locally equivalent to addition under a change of coordinate. We prove an $n$-valued analogue in the algebraic and formal settings. Over a field of characteristic zero, every associative algebraic $n$-valued monoid on $\mathbb P^1$ with a strong two-sided unit is commutative. Over a reduced commutative $\mathbb Q$-algebra, any one-dimensional formal $n$-valued group is commutative. We then classify $n$-valued formal groups over arbitrary $\mathbb Q$-algebras that are integral domains: for any $n$-valued formal group there is a unique divisor $m$ of $n$ such that the law is strongly isomorphic to the $n/m$-fold diagonal of the cyclic elementary $m$-valued law $\mathbb G_m$. This proves Kholodov's classification conjecture over integral domain $\mathbb Q$-algebras.

title: The geometric classification of Novikov-Poisson and Gelfand-Dorfman algebras
author: Zeyu Hao, Ivan Kaygorodov, Azamat Saydaliyev, Ziyi Zhang
description:
arXiv:2610.14010v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We give the geometric classification of complex 3-dimensional Novikov-Poisson and Gelfand-Dorfman algebras. In particular, we prove that the variety of complex 3-dimensional Novikov-Poisson algebras is 12-dimensional; it has 4 irreducible components and has no rigid algebras; the variety of complex 3-dimensional Gelfand-Dorfman algebras is 11-dimensional; it has 10 irreducible components and has 3 rigid algebras. As an additional result, we have the geometric classification of complex 3-dimensional Novikov algebras: it is 9-dimensional, and it has $4$ irreducible components with one rigid algebra.

title: Multiplicity-One Structure in Graded Zero-Divisor Graphs
author: M. Aijaz, Shahnawaz A. Rather, S Pirzada
description:
arXiv:2610.14003v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let \(H\) be a multiplicative group, \(R\) a commutative \(H\)-graded ring, and \(M\) a nonzero finitely generated gr-semisimple \(H\)-graded \(R\)-module. We assume that \(M\) admits a fixed decomposition into powers of gr-simple modules with pairwise distinct annihilators, each repeated block carrying the componentwise grading. For a nonzero homogeneous element \(x\), we compute the colon ideal \((Rx:M)\) and show that it is determined by the multiplicity-one blocks on which \(x\) has a nonzero component. This leads to the criterion \( x\leftrightarrow y \text{ if and only if } σ(x)\capσ(y)=\varnothing, \) where \(x\leftrightarrow y\) means that \(x\) and \(y\) are adjacent in \(Γ_H(M)\). Thus adjacency is governed by disjointness of multiplicity-one obstruction supports. The corresponding obstruction classes form a weighted disjointness structure: higher multiplicities affect the sizes of the classes, but not the adjacency relation between their supports. We use this description to study graph invariants, reconstruction, and Kneser-type layers, and, in the finite case, to obtain formulas for the obstruction-class sizes and a reduction of the adjacency spectrum.

title: Upper Bounds on the Comon Rank Gap of Real Symmetric Third-Order Tensors
author: Jianze Li
description:
arXiv:2610.14002v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $T$ be a nonzero real symmetric third-order tensor. Denote by $r(T)$ its CP rank, by $s(T)$ its symmetric rank, by $d(T)$ its essential dimension, and put $e(T)=r(T)-d(T)$. We establish two complementary upper bounds for the Comon rank gap $$Δ(T):= s(T)-r(T)\leq\min\{C_{ec}(e(T)),\ C_{dc}(d(T))\}.$$ The excess-controlled function $C_{ec}(e)$ is zero for $0\leq e\leq3$ and equals $9e-3$ for $e\geq4$. In particular, the equality $C_{ec}(e(T))=0$ for $0\leq e\leq3$ extends Friedland's flattening-rank criterion for real symmetric third-order tensors by two additional rank layers. The dimension-controlled function $C_{dc}(d)$ is zero for $d=0$, equals $(d^2-4d+10)/3$ for $1\leq d\leq18$, and equals $d^2/4+d/4+3/2$ for $d\geq19$. The excess estimate follows from the alternating equations and decomposable-bivector support geometry; a low-wedge descent gives the vanishing range $e\leq3$. The dimension estimate combines a transverse polar-completion bound with a shifted estimate for the maximum real Waring rank. Thus the two bounds measure different features of the same tensor and remain effective in complementary regimes.
